squawks.headline: German final HICP confirms annual inflation at 2.8%, in line with forecasts
squawks.detail: Final German HICP shows 2.8% year on year and -0.1% month on month, both matching forecasts and the previous readings. Final German CPI shows -0.2% month on month, also as expected.

squawks.headline: UK government backs approval of two major offshore wind projects with £1bn from the National Wealth Fund
squawks.detail: The UK government welcomed the approval of two large offshore wind projects. It confirmed a £12bn investment announcement by RWE and KKR, with £1bn of the financing package coming from the National Wealth Fund. It said more than 2,400 jobs would be supported during construction and operation.

squawks.headline: Japan's 10-year JGB yield extends rise to 2.795%, up 10.5bp, as longer maturities also climb
squawks.detail: Market reports put the 10-year JGB yield at 2.795%, up 10.5bp on the day. The 30-year yield rose 6.5bp to 3.935% and the 40-year rose 4bp to 4.100%.

squawks.headline: Oil rebounds from a two-month low as attacks on Hormuz shipping offset hopes of an Iran truce
squawks.detail: Reuters reports oil prices rose on Wednesday after falling to two-month lows in the previous session. It says traders were weighing hopes of de-escalation in the Iran war against continuing attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

squawks.headline: Japan's 10-year JGB yield rises 9bp to 2.780% and 5-year climbs 8.5bp to 2.185%
squawks.detail: The 10-year JGB yield extended its rise to 2.780%, up 9bp, after the 5-year yield earlier gained 8.5bp to 2.185%. Asian bond yields rose as bets on a Federal Reserve rate increase grew.

squawks.headline: Global bonds fall and dollar holds firm as hot US inflation raises risk of a half-point Fed hike
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that global bonds fell sharply after a hot US inflation print and hawkish central bank comments raised the chance of a half-point Federal Reserve rate rise next month. Equities held up and the dollar stayed firm.

squawks.headline: Japan PM Takaichi rules out fiscal measures that risk high inflation and expects BoJ to secure 2% goal
squawks.detail: Japan's Prime Minister said the government has no intention of adopting fiscal policies that could push inflation excessively higher. She said she expects the Bank of Japan to set suitable policy to reach its 2% inflation target sustainably.

squawks.headline: Rubio tells G7 counterparts Trump has opted to pressure Iran's regime rather than go to war or strike a deal
squawks.detail: Axios reports that the US Secretary of State told G7 peers the president has chosen a policy of pressure on Iran's government instead of either military action or an agreement.

squawks.headline: Japan's 10-year JGB yield rises 6.5bp to 2.755% and 2-year climbs 7bp to 1.845%
squawks.detail: Japanese government bond yields rose in early Tokyo trade, with the 10-year up 6.5bp at 2.755% and the 2-year up 7bp at 1.845%. Earlier in the session, 10-year JGB futures fell 0.56 point.

squawks.headline: UK investigation into the Budget leak covers details of bank tax measures
squawks.detail: British authorities are reported to be investigating a leak of Budget details on bank taxes. This adds to the earlier report that a government security group was looking into a possible leak of Budget measures.

squawks.headline: Fed's Paulson puts underlying US inflation at 2.5% to 3% and says policy must stay somewhat tight
squawks.detail: Fed official Paulson said the US economy has been more resilient than expected, with a firm and steady job market, and that the Fed has more work to do on inflation. She said the effect of AI and energy on inflation is difficult to measure and that the path of rates will depend on economic developments.

squawks.headline: NIESR calls on the Bank of England to raise rates from 4% to 5% and says inflation may not reach 2% target until 2030
squawks.detail: In its autumn report, the National Institute of Economic and Social Research says the Bank should raise Bank Rate sharply to 5% from 4%. It also says inflation may not return to the 2% target until 2030.

squawks.headline: Fed's Goolsbee says the US faces a genuine inflation challenge and all policy options remain open
squawks.detail: Speaking on PBS NewsHour, Fed official Goolsbee calls the CPI report borderline troubling and says his biggest concerns are high services inflation and emerging widespread overheating in prices. He says the Fed must bring inflation back to target and that the job market remains steady.

squawks.headline: Fed's Paulson backs further gradual rate rises and says CPI data show inflation is still a problem
squawks.detail: Fed official Paulson says policy must stay somewhat tight, the Fed has more work to do, and underlying inflation remains between 2.5% and 3%. He calls the economy more resilient than expected, with a firm and steady job market, and says he backed recent rate moves.

squawks.headline: Oil falls to $90 a barrel on hopes that talks will end the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine
squawks.detail: Semafor reports that oil fell to $90 a barrel after US President Trump played down the risk of renewed conflict with Iran and talks between Kyiv, Moscow and Washington began.

squawks.headline: Poland's Orlen ends a long-term LNG supply contract with QatarEnergy, citing ongoing force majeure
squawks.detail: Orlen, Poland's largest energy group, said on Tuesday it had terminated one of its two long-term LNG supply contracts with QatarEnergy. It said an ongoing force majeure had left the supplier unable to meet its delivery obligations.

squawks.headline: UK ministers reject Botley West, which would have been Britain's largest solar farm
squawks.detail: The UK government turned down the Oxfordshire project, saying it would do substantial harm to the green belt and to Blenheim Palace, the FT reports.

squawks.headline: US Senate advances permitting reform bill meant to speed up building of energy infrastructure
squawks.detail: Semafor reports that the US Senate has moved forward major permitting reforms designed to speed up construction of energy infrastructure. The outlet says the Democrats' win in last week's midterms has added momentum to the reform.

squawks.headline: Fed's Bowman says inflation is not trending lower and the Fed must consider the pace and timeline of its response
squawks.detail: Fed Governor Bowman said that inflation not moving down should give policymakers pause. She added that the Fed needs to weigh how fast to act on it and over what timeline.

squawks.headline: Fed's Bowman likens possible action on inflation in coming months to last year's gradual cuts followed by a pause
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve Governor Bowman said the Fed cut rates gradually last year, paused and then resumed, and that it may take a similar approach to addressing inflation in the coming months.

squawks.headline: Fed's Waller warns a half-point rate rise in December may be necessary
squawks.detail: Waller's warning came on the same day Fed's Logan backed at least two more quarter-point rises, after a stronger-than-expected US CPI print. Market wraps report that US stocks and Treasuries fell, with short-dated Treasuries hit hardest, while the dollar rose and money markets priced in a December move larger than 25bp.

squawks.headline: Fed's Bowman says AI will raise worker productivity, create new jobs and remove less essential ones
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman commented on the labour market effects of artificial intelligence in remarks on Tuesday.

squawks.headline: Fed's Bowman says the Fed is collecting data on AI debt counterparties and stresses open communication with the Treasury
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve Governor Bowman said the Fed is seeking data on counterparties to AI-related debt, and that keeping lines of communication open with the US Treasury is critically important.

squawks.headline: Fed's Bowman says she would need AI and Middle East risks to ease before being confident inflation falls next year
squawks.detail: Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman said she is shifting her focus to inflation and that longer-term inflation expectations remain very well anchored. She added that expectations are an important input but do not necessarily drive her thinking.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy welcomes recent US messages and sees a change in approach from envoys Witkoff and Kushner
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy, speaking in Copenhagen, said he was very pleased with recent messages from the US side and saw changes in the approach of US envoys Witkoff and Kushner. The remarks follow the Abu Dhabi talks on ending the war.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says a new European security architecture is on the agenda at the Abu Dhabi talks
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy, speaking in Copenhagen, said a new European security architecture is among the topics in the Abu Dhabi talks on ending the war.

squawks.headline: Fed's Bowman estimates October core PCE at 3.3% and says the Fed must weigh the costs of further tightening as financial conditions tighten
squawks.detail: In a speech to the Council on Foreign Relations, Federal Reserve Governor Bowman said core PCE probably rose 3.3% in October because of energy prices and AI-related demand, and that she expects it to move closer to 2% next year as those shocks unwind. She also said financial conditions have tightened, and that the labour market has improved but is not tight and is not adding to inflation.

squawks.headline: Fed's Bowman says persistent inflation and a firming labour market mean there is still work to do
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve Governor Bowman cited persistent inflation and firmer labour market conditions in her remarks.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine is ready to discuss territory and to meet Putin, but doubts Russia is ready for a leaders' meeting
squawks.detail: Ukraine's president said Kyiv will request a meeting of leaders and is prepared to talk about territory. He added that Ukraine and Russia discussed a possible prisoner exchange of 1000 for 1000 or 1500 for 1500.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says Europe must settle this month who will represent it in Ukraine peace negotiations
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said in Copenhagen that a decision on Europe's representative in the negotiations is needed this month. He also said he hopes the US Congress will act more decisively.

squawks.headline: Iran's Fars says the South Pars platform hit by fire produces 14.5m cubic metres of the field's 700m cubic metres of gas
squawks.detail: Iran's Fars news agency gave the output of the platform at the South Pars gas field where a fire was earlier reported to be under control. It put the platform's production at 14.5m cubic metres of gas, out of a field total of 700m cubic metres.

squawks.headline: Fire on a platform at Iran's South Pars gas field is under control, Iranian media report; cause under investigation
squawks.detail: Iran's Fars news agency reports the fire is under control. Iranian reports say the platform produces 14.5m cubic metres of gas out of the field's total 700m, and that a gas leak or an operational incident are the two possible causes.

squawks.headline: Fed's Schmid says US hiring has been fairly robust and demand is strong
squawks.detail: Fed's Schmid said recent US hiring has been fairly robust, demand is strong and interest rates are not holding activity back. He added that a lot of data is due before the Fed's December meeting.

squawks.headline: Fed's Schmid expects instant payments to overtake digital asset structures
squawks.detail: Kansas City Fed President Schmid said instant payment systems are likely to leapfrog digital asset structures. The remarks were about payments, not monetary policy.

squawks.headline: Fed's Schmid says inflation is his main concern
squawks.detail: Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid said inflation is foremost in his thinking, in further remarks on 10 November.

squawks.headline: Fed's Schmid calls policy rate fairly accommodative and finds no restriction outside housing
squawks.detail: Kansas City Fed President Schmid said US hiring had been quite robust lately and demand was strong. He said rates gave no cause for hesitation, and that apart from the housing market he could find no sign that policy was restrictive.

squawks.headline: US envoy Kushner calls the day's Ukraine talks constructive and says the US is working to end the war
squawks.detail: Kushner said the US was acting at President Trump's direction to end the war and to agree security arrangements for a sovereign Ukraine and lasting peace in Europe.

squawks.headline: Fed's Schmid sees some concerning price trends beneath the energy-driven inflation story
squawks.detail: Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid said there are some worrying trends in prices underlying the effect of energy. The remarks come on the day US October CPI came in above forecasts.

squawks.headline: Qatar's PM tells G7 foreign ministers Doha has won at least two weeks for diplomacy towards a US-Iran understanding
squawks.detail: According to the Jerusalem Post, Qatari Prime Minister Al Thani told G7 foreign ministers meeting in Paris that Doha had secured a window of at least two weeks to pursue diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran.

squawks.headline: Bank of Canada minutes keep further rate hikes on the table and say policy can stop energy prices becoming generalised inflation
squawks.detail: Minutes of the deliberations before the Bank of Canada's 28 October rate announcement show the Governing Council saying uncertainty over rates did not mean inaction, and that rising cost pressures would eventually show up in core inflation. Members also said inflation expectations may have become more sensitive to recent price changes, and that businesses face higher costs for non-energy imports such as semiconductors.

squawks.headline: BoE's Lombardelli sees a case for another rate rise in the near term, citing high energy prices and resilient UK growth
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Bank of England Deputy Governor Clare Lombardelli said high energy prices and the resilience of UK growth support a further rate increase in the near term. She did not rule out back-to-back rate rises.

squawks.headline: US EIA holds 2026 world oil demand at 102.4m bpd, cuts 2027 to 104.4m bpd and trims its 2027 world output forecast
squawks.detail: The US Energy Information Administration's Short-Term Energy Outlook keeps 2026 world oil demand at 102.4m bpd and lowers 2027 to 104.4m bpd from 104.6m bpd. It raises 2026 world oil output to 101.7m bpd from 101.1m bpd and cuts 2027 to 108.4m bpd from 109.6m bpd.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation puts real per-person public services spending growth at 1.7% a year from 2023-24 to 2028-29
squawks.detail: In its Budget analysis, the Resolution Foundation says day-to-day spending is growing moderately in this Parliament. It puts public services spending growth at 1.7% a year in real per-person terms between 2023-24 and 2028-29, which it says is similar to the two most recent periods under Conservative governments.

squawks.headline: New US 10-year notes to carry a 5% coupon, the highest since 2006
squawks.detail: A market commentator reported the coupon after the $42bn US 10-year note auction, which had already been reported as tailing.

squawks.headline: US $42bn 10-year note auction tails by 1bp at 5.020% high yield; bid-to-cover falls to 2.46 from 2.770
squawks.detail: The US Treasury sold $42bn of 10-year notes at a high yield of 5.020%, against 5.300% at the previous sale, with a 1bp tail and 95.17% of bids awarded at the high. Primary dealers took 9.8%, direct bidders 29.0% and indirect bidders 61.2%.

squawks.headline: US 10-year when-issued yield stands at 5.010% ahead of $42bn Treasury auction
squawks.detail: Ahead of the US Treasury's $42 billion 10-year note auction, the 10-year when-issued yield was reported at 5.010%.

squawks.headline: EU's Costa says Ukraine financing will be taken up at the 26-27 November EU summit once the Commission sends its proposal
squawks.detail: European Council President Costa told German Chancellor Merz in a letter that Ukraine financing will be on the agenda of the EU summit on 26-27 November. He said this will follow receipt of a proposal from the European Commission.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lane expects second-round effects and says headline inflation could fall as energy reverses while underlying inflation rises
squawks.detail: ECB chief economist Lane said underlying inflation has not yet moved, consistent with the usual delayed response, and that it guides inflation one year ahead. He added that energy prices are already reversing and it would be surprising if there were no second-round effects.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lane says the ECB needs a tool for dealing with multiple equilibria in bond markets
squawks.detail: ECB chief economist Philip Lane said it is important for the ECB to have an instrument for situations where bond markets could settle at more than one equilibrium. The remarks follow his earlier comments on forward guidance.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lane sets a high bar for directional forward guidance and says a dot plot would sit poorly with the ECB's consensus approach
squawks.detail: ECB chief economist Philip Lane said the Governing Council places great weight on consensus, which would make publishing rate projections in the style of a dot plot difficult. He added that he would set a high bar for directional forward guidance at present.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham rules out dynamic alignment of the UK with EU financial services rules
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Burnham rejected dynamically aligning the UK with EU rules on financial services, a market news account reported. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Ukraine's foreign minister says Kyiv awaits Russia's reply on Black Sea ceasefire proposals and is not optimistic on progress
squawks.detail: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Sybiha also said the cost of the war will be higher in 2027 and called on allies to agree long-term funding commitments this year. He said he asked US Secretary of State Rubio to speed up deliveries of air-defence interceptors as Russia attacks energy infrastructure.

squawks.headline: US EIA raises Brent forecasts to $97.44/bbl for 2026 and $85.78/bbl for 2027
squawks.detail: The US Energy Information Administration's Short-Term Energy Outlook raises its 2026 Brent average forecast from $96.32/bbl and its 2027 forecast from $83.74/bbl. It puts 2026 world oil output at 101.7m bpd, up from 101.1m bpd, and cuts its 2027 figure to 108.4m bpd from 109.6m bpd, with 2026 world demand unchanged at 102.4m bpd.

squawks.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield reported up 15bp on the day after October CPI beat
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports the 10-year US Treasury yield has risen 15bp on the day, taking it back to 5%. The move follows a stronger-than-expected October CPI reading of 0.4% m/m.

squawks.headline: Canada's Carney says some difficult areas remain in trade talks with the US
squawks.detail: Canadian Prime Minister Carney said Canada has settled its red lines with the US on cultural questions. He also said Canada does not need a contested tax on large web companies.

squawks.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield climbs back to 5% for the first time in 12 days
squawks.detail: A market news feed reports the US 10-year Treasury yield back at 5%, the first time in 12 days. The move follows the October US CPI release, which came in above forecasts earlier in the session.

squawks.headline: Iran's Rezaei says there are no US-Iran negotiations under way and calls US claims of continuing talks fabricated
squawks.detail: Iran's security chief Rezaei says no negotiations are currently taking place between Tehran and Washington, and that Iran has asked the US for a clear and explicit response to its conditions. He repeats that the Strait of Hormuz will stay closed until the US meets Iran's seven conditions.

squawks.headline: Iranian officials say the Strait of Hormuz will stay closed until Iran's seven conditions are met
squawks.detail: Major General Rezaei said Hormuz will not reopen until Iran's seven conditions are met, and the Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council said the same. Rezaei separately repeated that the US has not yet given a clear response to the conditions.

squawks.headline: Iran's Rezaei says Iran has set seven conditions and the US has not yet given a clear response
squawks.detail: Iranian Major General Rezaei said Iran had laid down seven conditions and was still waiting for a clear US answer, and called the American response deceptive, Fars News reported. He also said US claims that talks with Iran are continuing are meant to bring oil prices down.

squawks.headline: Fed's Logan puts policy rate at least 50bp below a mildly restrictive level and sees a pause after two more hikes
squawks.detail: Dallas Fed President Logan said accommodative policy is adding to inflation pressure, put the real fed funds rate at 78bp and said pausing to assess after two more increases would be logical. She said inflation is well above the 2% target, that price pressures go beyond energy and tariffs, and that the labour market is balanced to slightly tight.

squawks.headline: Traders fully price two 25bp Bank of England rate hikes by March
squawks.detail: Market pricing now fully reflects two quarter-point increases in Bank Rate by March, a market commentary account reports.

squawks.headline: Fed's Logan says at least two more 25bp hikes are needed and that faster rate rises may be needed this winter
squawks.detail: Dallas Fed President Logan said in a speech that the Fed's policy rate is at least 50bp below a modestly restrictive level, that the real Fed funds rate is 78bp, and that it would make sense to pause and assess after two more hikes. She said inflation is trending meaningfully above the 2% goal, price pressures go beyond wartime energy disruptions and tariffs, and the labour market is balanced and even tightening a bit.

squawks.headline: Netanyahu says Israel will soon face international pressure to accept a nuclear Iran and to pull back from security zones
squawks.detail: Israel's prime minister told the Knesset that Iran is working to renew its nuclear threat and has not dropped its aim of destroying Israel. He said Israel faces pressure to give up its gains in Syria, Lebanon and Gaza, and called for a national unity government.

squawks.headline: Netanyahu tells Knesset Iran is reviving its nuclear programme and says overthrowing its regime is the only lasting solution
squawks.detail: In a speech to the Knesset, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu said Iran is working to revive its nuclear programme after the immediate threat was removed. He said the only way to remove the threat permanently is to overthrow the regime.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy calls Abu Dhabi talks constructive and substantive; trilateral talks set to continue tomorrow
squawks.detail: Ukraine's president says negotiators discussed the substance of security guarantees for Ukraine in detail. He says he has given his team instructions for tomorrow's trilateral round and for talks in the coming days with US and European representatives.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister says diplomacy, not military action or sanctions, will end the war and denies reports of a Rezaei-Vance meeting
squawks.detail: Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi said the conflict will be resolved through diplomacy and acceptance of Iran's conditions, not by military action or sanctions. He also called reports of a meeting between security chief Rezaei and US Vice President Vance baseless media speculation.

squawks.headline: ECB's Nagel calls the fall in energy prices since the US midterms positive and says France must address its finances
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Nagel said action will be taken to return inflation to 2%, and that market expectations matter but are not the main influence on policy. He also said France needs to deal with its fiscal problems.

squawks.headline: US 2-year Treasury yield heads for its biggest one-day rise since April 2025
squawks.detail: A market report says the US 2-year yield is on course for its largest single-session increase since April 2025, after the October CPI release.

squawks.headline: ECB's Nagel says a December rate rise is clearly needed and sees no risk of fiscal dominance
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Nagel said the ECB will do what is needed to bring inflation back to 2%, called the fall in energy prices since the US midterms good news, and said market expectations matter but are not the deciding factor. He also said France must address its fiscal challenges.

squawks.headline: Two-year yield reported up 17.4bp on the day, with the 30-year yield up 6.3bp
squawks.detail: A market newswire reports the two-year yield up 17.4bp and the 30-year up 6.3bp on the day; the post does not name the market. It follows the October US CPI release.

squawks.headline: UK government security group investigates a possible leak of Budget measures that may have moved markets
squawks.detail: A letter published by the Treasury Select Committee confirms the investigation, which is being led by a government security group. It concerns a Bloomberg report on a bank tax published just before the Budget, and the committee's chair, Meg Hillier, was reported to have responded with exasperation.

squawks.headline: IFS says Conservative welfare proposals imply large but uncertain reductions in benefit spending
squawks.detail: The Institute for Fiscal Studies published a response from its researcher Tom Waters assessing the opposition Conservatives' welfare plans. It says the plans imply substantial cuts to benefit spending, though the scale is uncertain.

squawks.headline: White House adviser Hassett calls US CPI report disappointing and says energy prices are feeding into the data
squawks.detail: White House senior adviser Hassett called the October US CPI report disappointing. In an interview with Fox Business, he said higher energy prices were feeding through into the data.

squawks.headline: SNB's Martin expects moderate Swiss growth over the coming quarters
squawks.detail: Swiss National Bank official Martin said the Swiss economy is expected to grow moderately over the next few quarters.

squawks.headline: Houthis deny attacking East-West pipeline in Medina region and say their strike was only on the Riyadh section
squawks.detail: Yemen's Houthis denied attacking the Saudi East-West oil pipeline in the Medina region. They said they attacked the pipeline only in the Riyadh area.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says Abu Dhabi talks covered a prisoner exchange and security guarantees
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said he had received reports from his negotiators after the trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi. He said the talks covered a prisoner exchange and security guarantees.

squawks.headline: Houthis say they attacked Aramco's Abqaiq facility and pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline
squawks.detail: In a statement, Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and an Aramco facility at Abqaiq. They said the attacks also targeted King Khalid International Airport and a financial centre in Riyadh, as well as troops. None of the posts reports a market reaction.

squawks.headline: Houthis say they have carried out several operations against Saudi Arabia
squawks.detail: The Houthis announced several operations against Saudi Arabia, according to a market news account. The report did not give details of targets or say whether markets moved.

squawks.headline: ECB's Cipollone warns the digital euro could be delayed if legislative talks drag on
squawks.detail: ECB Executive Board member Piero Cipollone warned on Tuesday that the digital euro could be delayed if talks on it continue for too long. He made no reported comment on interest rates.

squawks.headline: Rubio rejects negotiating over Lebanon with Iran as part of US-Iran talks
squawks.detail: US Secretary of State Rubio questioned why the US would negotiate with Iran over Lebanon. He made the remarks during comments on the US-Iran talks, which Qatar is mediating.

squawks.headline: Prediction markets price a 12% chance of a Fed hike above 25bp in December and 85% for a 25bp move
squawks.detail: Natixis says the stronger-than-expected October US CPI and hawkish Fed remarks have put a larger December hike in play. Prediction markets give a 12% chance of a move above 25bp and 85% for a standard 25bp increase.

squawks.headline: Rubio says Trump has decided there is currently no need for US military operations against Iran and denies a stalemate
squawks.detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said President Trump had judged that military operations against Iran are not needed at present. He also said the situation with Iran is not a stalemate.

squawks.headline: US October supercore CPI rises 0.4% m/m, against 0.42% previously
squawks.detail: Supercore CPI rose 0.4% on the month, compared with 0.42% in the previous reading. Gold and copper were reported extending losses after the inflation report.

squawks.headline: Rubio says Iran's conditions for a deal are absurd and the sides are not close; US rejects reparations demands
squawks.detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said the US is ready to negotiate with Iran if a deal is possible but will not accept a bad one, and that Iran's demand for reparations will not be met. He also said economic pressure on Iran will get even worse.

squawks.headline: Traders increase bets on a 50bp Fed rate hike in December after the October US CPI release
squawks.detail: Market commentary reports traders adding to positions for a half-point Fed hike next month. This follows the October US CPI rise of 0.4% m/m, which was above forecast.

squawks.headline: Rubio says US aims eventually to widen trilateral Ukraine talks to include European countries
squawks.detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said the goal is at some point to bring Europeans into the US-Russia-Ukraine talks. He said US and European goals on Ukraine and Russia are the same and that Europe is at the table.

squawks.headline: Rubio calls Abu Dhabi Russia-Ukraine talks very productive but says a deal will not come within 48 hours
squawks.detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said the Abu Dhabi talks on Russia and Ukraine were very productive, though much work remains. He said the US wants Europeans at the table soon.

squawks.headline: US 2- to 5-year Treasury yields rise at least 10bp on the day after October CPI beats forecasts
squawks.detail: Traders kept pricing for a December Fed hike at 100%.

squawks.headline: Rubio says economic pressure on Iran is working and major combat operations are no longer needed
squawks.detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said he told G7 counterparts that the economic campaign against Iran is working well enough that President Trump has no need to carry out major combat operations.

squawks.headline: US October CPI rises 0.4% m/m, above 0.3% forecast; core CPI up 0.3%, above 0.2% forecast
squawks.detail: US consumer prices rose 0.4% month on month in October, compared with a 0.3% forecast and 0.6% in the previous month. Core CPI rose 0.3%, against a 0.2% forecast and unchanged from the previous month's 0.3%.

squawks.headline: BoE's Lombardelli says monetary policy is less restrictive than the Bank had thought
squawks.detail: Bank of England Deputy Governor Clare Lombardelli said policy is less restrictive than previously judged. In the same remarks she said some European countries, including France, face very difficult debt trajectories.

squawks.headline: BoE's Lombardelli says long-term inflation expectations remain well anchored, with no sign of de-anchoring
squawks.detail: Bank of England Deputy Governor Clare Lombardelli said long-term inflation expectations are very well anchored and the Bank does not see them de-anchoring. She made the remarks during her appearance on 10 November.

squawks.headline: UK foreign minister calls for a full diplomatic push to end the Iran conflict
squawks.detail: The UK foreign minister called for a comprehensive diplomatic effort to bring the Iran conflict to an end.

squawks.headline: US Defense Secretary Hegseth says the US is ready to act if Iran makes a wrong move and can strike its nuclear sites if needed
squawks.detail: US Defense Secretary Hegseth said US forces remain ready to respond to Iran and that the US can see Iran's nuclear sites and could take action if necessary.

squawks.headline: BoE's Lombardelli does not rule out back-to-back rate hikes and says every MPC meeting is live
squawks.detail: BoE Deputy Governor Lombardelli said she would not rule a hike in December or February in or out, and that the December vote will depend on the Middle East outlook, pricing and the labour market. She also said the UK's natural rate of unemployment may be somewhat higher than before.

squawks.headline: US ADP weekly employment change rises to 19.75K from 16.75K
squawks.detail: ADP's weekly employment change for the period to 24 October came in at 19.75K, up from 16.75K previously. No forecast was given.

squawks.headline: BoE's Lombardelli says wage growth is easing more slowly than hoped
squawks.detail: BoE Deputy Governor Lombardelli said pay is not slowing as quickly as hoped. She also said it is very hard to tell whether the UK economy has become more resilient to price shocks or is close to the limit of what households and firms can absorb.

squawks.headline: BoE's Lombardelli says UK economy may have less slack than the Bank's central view, perhaps 0-1% rather than 1%
squawks.detail: Bank of England Deputy Governor Clare Lombardelli said spare capacity in the UK economy may be smaller than the Bank's central estimate of 1%, putting it at perhaps 0-1%.

squawks.headline: US Defense Secretary Hegseth says the US controls the Strait of Hormuz and over 80% of Iran's nuclear industrial base is gone
squawks.detail: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made the remarks at a press conference, where he also said Iran started the war.

squawks.headline: Germany's Merz says the EU budget needs new priorities in defence and competitiveness
squawks.detail: German Chancellor Merz said the next EU budget must set new priorities in defence and competitiveness. He added that supporting Ukraine is a collective task for the European Union.

squawks.headline: First day of Russia-US-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi ends after 4.5 hours, reports say
squawks.detail: Russian reports say the Russian, US and Ukrainian delegations finished their first day of negotiations in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday. The session reportedly lasted 4.5 hours.

squawks.headline: Reuters poll: all 101 economists expect the Fed to raise rates in December to 4.00%-4.25%
squawks.detail: In the Reuters poll, 56 of the 101 economists expect the fed funds rate to peak at 4.00%-4.25% in this hiking cycle, and 29 of 37 said the risk to their medium-term US inflation view has not changed since the midterm elections. Prediction markets are reported to price an 87% chance of a 25bp hike, against 9% for a hold.

squawks.headline: Germany's Merz says EU budget talks must not lead to reduced support for Ukraine
squawks.detail: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said, in the context of EU budget discussions, that support for Ukraine cannot be scaled back.

squawks.headline: BoE's Lombardelli says conditions for persistent medium-term inflation are taking shape and risks remain to the upside
squawks.detail: Bank of England Deputy Governor Clare Lombardelli said the balance of risks to inflation is still to the upside. She added that conditions for persistent inflationary dynamics over the medium term are starting to crystallise.

squawks.headline: Iran reportedly agrees to US demands to cut its highly enriched uranium levels, Al Hadath says
squawks.detail: Al Hadath cited sources as saying Iran has accepted US demands to reduce its stocks of highly enriched uranium. The report has not been officially confirmed, and no market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: BoE's Lombardelli sees upside inflation risks as the energy shock proves more persistent, raising the chance of second-round effects
squawks.detail: BoE Deputy Governor Lombardelli said the energy shock has become more persistent, that high energy costs that last longer will push firms harder to restore margins, and that the balance of inflation risks lies to the upside. She also described the labour market as stuck in low gear.

squawks.headline: Ukrainian strikes since late October have reportedly reduced Russia's oil refining capacity by about 30%
squawks.detail: Two industry sources say Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries since late October have reduced Russia's oil processing capacity by about 30%. According to the sources, actual processing volumes are down by about 200,000 tons per day.

squawks.headline: BoE is reportedly considering changes to how it carries out its remaining APF gilt sales
squawks.detail: A market commentary account reported that the Bank of England is weighing an adjustment to how it conducts the remaining gilt sales from the Asset Purchase Facility. The post gave no further details or timing.

squawks.headline: Oil is more than 20% below its late-October peak as markets bet on the Iran conflict winding down, Reuters says
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that oil prices have fallen more than 20% from their late-October peak, with markets betting that the Iran conflict is winding down.

squawks.headline: France and Ukraine welcome US efforts at the Abu Dhabi Ukraine peace talks
squawks.detail: Paris said France and Ukraine welcome the US role in the trilateral talks under way in Abu Dhabi. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: EU says the US should respect pharmaceutical trade commitments made in their August joint statement
squawks.detail: An EU spokesperson said on Tuesday that the commitments on trade in the pharmaceutical sector set out in the EU-US joint statement in August should be respected.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation publishes analysis of how the Budget's abolition of the gas standing charge affects households
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation has published an analysis of how scrapping the gas standing charge, announced in the October 2026 Budget, affects different households. It says the measure has drawn less attention than the £100 Household Energy Payment.

squawks.headline: Lavrov says Russia rejects European calls for an immediate Ukraine ceasefire and accuses Brussels of stalling
squawks.detail: Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov said Moscow will not accept European demands for an immediate ceasefire in Ukraine. He added that Russia cannot and does not want to stop the US from talking to European partners on Ukraine, although it does not see that format as the best approach.

squawks.headline: US NFIB small business optimism index slips to 97.8, below the 98.2 forecast
squawks.detail: The NFIB small business optimism index was 97.8, against a forecast of 98.2 and a previous reading of 97.9.

squawks.headline: Russia, US and Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi reportedly restart after being suspended
squawks.detail: Reports say the trilateral negotiations between Russia, the United States and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi have resumed after a suspension. No further details or market reaction were reported.

squawks.headline: Budget keeps the Local Housing Allowance freeze in place into 2027-28, Resolution Foundation says
squawks.detail: According to the Resolution Foundation, more than a million families lose out from extending the freeze, and 91% of them are in the bottom half of the income distribution. The think tank says the Budget's Your First Home scheme will help a small number of renters buy.

squawks.headline: Iran's IRGC navy says two tankers caught fire after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: Iranian state media and Tasnim carried the IRGC navy's report of the two tankers catching fire in the strait. The inputs report no market reaction.

squawks.headline: Qatar says its US-Iran mediation continues and both sides have responded positively
squawks.detail: Qatar said its efforts to mediate between Iran and the US are continuing, and that both sides have reacted positively to the mediation.

squawks.headline: Fed's Waller says he doesn't think any Fed colleagues believe rates are at the right level
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he does not believe any of his Fed colleagues think policy rates are currently in the right place.

squawks.headline: ECB's Kazaks says more tightening may be needed if the energy shock persists and sees no need to slow or end QT
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Kazaks also said inflation is likely to go significantly above 4% in 2027. He described stress in French bonds as a repricing of fiscal risk.

squawks.headline: ECB's Kazaks says monetary policy still needs some hawkish edge but must avoid hurting the economy too much
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Kazaks said policy should keep some hawkish edge. He also said inflation must be brought under control without doing too much damage to the economy.

squawks.headline: Fed's Waller says reversing the three insurance cuts is the minimum needed but rules out hikes of 150bp to 200bp
squawks.detail: Fed Governor Waller said that at the very least the Fed needs to undo its three insurance rate cuts. He added that he is not super hawkish, does not want to slam the economy down and that the Fed will not raise rates by 150bp or 200bp.

squawks.headline: UK 30-year gilt auction draws 3.75 times cover at an average yield of 5.54%
squawks.detail: The 30-year gilt sale was covered 3.75 times, down from 3.84 at the previous auction. The average yield was 5.54%, compared with 5.517% last time.

squawks.headline: ECB's Kazaks says policy must stop energy inflation spilling over and gradual action is still appropriate
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Kazaks said policymakers must stay vigilant and cautious. He said it remains appropriate to act gradually and that policy must keep energy inflation from spreading further.

squawks.headline: Fed's Waller says real rates must rise to keep policy restrictive and higher rates are needed to bear down on inflation
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve Governor Waller said real interest rates need to rise to keep monetary policy as restrictive as it is now. He added that the Fed needs to raise rates to put downward pressure on inflation.

squawks.headline: EU says European partners, Ukraine and US agree any Ukraine deal must respect sovereignty and include credible security guarantees
squawks.detail: In an EU statement after a coordination meeting ahead of talks with Russia, European partners, Ukraine and the US said they share the goal of a practical and mutually reinforcing security framework, and that dealing with post-war security concerns and reducing the risk of conflict is essential. Participants said they will keep working closely together throughout the negotiations.

squawks.headline: Kremlin declines to predict chances of progress at Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks while negotiations continue
squawks.detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said the Russian delegation in Abu Dhabi will decide how often and in what format to report to President Putin, depending on how the negotiations progress. He declined to give a view on the prospects for progress towards peace while talks are under way.

squawks.headline: Canada reimposes sanctions on 11 Iranian entities
squawks.detail: Canada's foreign minister, Anita Anand, announced that sanctions are being reimposed on 11 Iranian entities. She noted that Canada had delisted Iranian entities in 2016 after Iran's progress under the 2015 Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action.

squawks.headline: Fed's Waller backs a December hike and is open to 50bp if October core CPI is 0.3% or more; traders fully price 25bp
squawks.detail: Fed Governor Waller said he would back a quarter-point hike in December even if October CPI improves on September, and that a half-point move may be needed if October core CPI comes in around 0.3% or higher. He called US inflation too high, flagged concern about how widespread price rises are and the risk of a more persistent energy shock, and described the labour market as solid; traders were reported to have moved to fully price a 25bp December hike.

squawks.headline: BoE's Breeden says firms have become very good at adapting to cost shocks
squawks.detail: Bank of England Deputy Governor Sarah Breeden, a member of the MPC, said businesses are now very good at adjusting to cost shocks. No remarks on the rate outlook were reported in the post.

squawks.headline: Brent crude drops below $90 a barrel for the first time since August
squawks.detail: A market news account reported Brent futures falling below $90 a barrel on Tuesday morning, the lowest since August.

squawks.headline: US gasoline price falls below $4 a gallon for the first time since July
squawks.detail: A market commentator reports that US gasoline has dropped under $4 per gallon, its first time below that level since July.

squawks.headline: Riksbank's Jansson says policy normalisation remains relatively cautious
squawks.detail: Riksbank Deputy Governor Jansson said Sweden's current policy normalisation is still relatively cautious.

squawks.headline: Ukraine's chief negotiator confirms trilateral talks with the US and Russia are under way; Russia's Medinsky hopes for progress
squawks.detail: Ukraine's chief negotiator Umerov said the talks with the US and Russia have moved to a trilateral format, with an agenda covering an end to hostilities and peace. Russia's lead negotiator Medinsky said he hopes the updated Russian delegation will help move things towards peace.

squawks.headline: BoE's Lombardelli calls December MPC meeting live for a further rate hike and says the Iran war is pushing up unemployment
squawks.detail: In an interview with the Guardian, Bank of England Deputy Governor Clare Lombardelli said the December MPC meeting is live for considering another rate rise. She said the Iran war has raised energy prices, clouded the outlook and driven up unemployment, and that young people are bearing the brunt of a sluggish economy.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lane says a December hike would be prudent if the data hold, and sees inflation slightly above 4% at year-end
squawks.detail: ECB chief economist Philip Lane said inflation is likely to end the year a little above 4%, with more to come before the peak, and he expects core and food inflation to pick up. He also said oil prices could move a lot before the December meeting, that he would like markets to reprice in line with the wider macro picture, that Europe's resilience is reassuring, and that France's fiscal problems need to be fixed in Paris.

squawks.headline: Russia, Ukraine and US trilateral talks reportedly begin in Abu Dhabi
squawks.detail: Reports say three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US have started in Abu Dhabi. Ukraine's Umerov said the delegation's first meeting is with European, NATO and EU representatives and US envoys Witkoff and Kushner.

squawks.headline: Canada's foreign minister hopes for progress on US tariffs after the midterm elections
squawks.detail: Canada's foreign minister said she hopes for progress on US tariffs once the US midterm elections are over. No timetable or specific measures were reported.

squawks.headline: Brent crude futures drop 2% to $90.66 a barrel
squawks.detail: Brent crude futures were reported down 2% at $90.66 a barrel in early European trading on 10 November.

squawks.headline: Ukraine peace talks get under way in Abu Dhabi, with US, Ukrainian and European delegations meeting
squawks.detail: Market commentary accounts report that talks have begun in Abu Dhabi and that the US delegation is meeting Ukrainian and European delegations. No market reaction is reported.

squawks.headline: Norway's October underlying CPI slows to 2.7% y/y, matching forecasts and down from 3.0%
squawks.detail: Norway's underlying inflation rose 0.3% m/m in October, against a forecast of 0.4% and 0.2% the previous month. Headline CPI was 3.6% y/y, below the 3.7% estimate.

squawks.headline: Norway's October CPI rises 3.6% y/y, below the 3.7% forecast and up from 3.4%
squawks.detail: Norwegian consumer prices rose 0.3% on the month, after 0.5% the previous month. The annual rate of 3.6% came in a little below the 3.7% forecast and above the previous 3.4%.

squawks.headline: ECB's Moulin expects ECB policy continuity if Knot or de Cos becomes president
squawks.detail: ECB official Moulin said he expects continuity at the central bank if either Knot or de Cos takes over.

squawks.headline: ADNOC CFO says LNG exports through Hormuz are still below pre-conflict levels despite month-on-month improvement
squawks.detail: ADNOC's chief financial officer said LNG cargoes leaving the Strait of Hormuz are improving each month but have not yet returned to pre-conflict levels. He added that the company has made no decisions on alternative LNG export facilities.

squawks.headline: ECB's Moulin says there are positive signs on energy prices
squawks.detail: ECB official Moulin said on 10 November that the central bank sees positive signs on energy prices.

squawks.headline: France says Europeans will attend Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks, rules out European security talks with Russia before a ceasefire
squawks.detail: France's foreign minister said European representatives will take part in the Ukraine-Russia talks in Abu Dhabi. France also said there will be no discussions with Russia on European security until a ceasefire is in place and peace in Ukraine is secured.

squawks.headline: US crude futures fall 2% to $85.11 a barrel
squawks.detail: US oil futures were reported down 2% at $85.11 a barrel in early trading on 10 November.

squawks.headline: BoE Deputy Governor Lombardelli does not rule out a December rate hike but says she needs more information
squawks.detail: Lombardelli says she would not exclude a December rate rise but does not yet have enough information, according to The Guardian. She also says hiring in the UK labour market has fallen off sharply without much sign of redundancies, and that young people are being hurt by a low-gear economy.

squawks.headline: Thames Water creditors ready a 'final' offer as PM Burnham weighs whether to nationalise the company, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Thames Water's creditors are preparing what they describe as a final offer. It says the prime minister has been reluctant to take the company into state ownership despite having supported the idea earlier.

squawks.headline: Laden LNG tanker exits from the Strait of Hormuz hit their highest monthly level in October since the Iran war began
squawks.detail: Reuters cites vessel tracking data showing the monthly count of laden LNG tankers leaving the Strait of Hormuz reached its highest in October since the US-Iran conflict disrupted shipping.

squawks.headline: US military moves aircraft out of a second UK base after an Iranian threat, WSJ reports
squawks.detail: The Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that the US military evacuated aircraft from a UK airbase on Monday following a threat from Iran.

squawks.headline: China's October crude imports reach their highest since March but are down 13.3% y/y
squawks.detail: Official Chinese data show October crude oil imports fell 13.3% from a year earlier but were the highest since March, after the war on Iran disrupted Middle East supplies.

squawks.headline: Japan's 30-year JGB auction tail widens to 0.35 from 0.16; 30-year yield rises 2.5bp to 3.865% afterwards
squawks.detail: The tail at Japan's 30-year government bond sale widened to 0.35, from 0.16 at the previous auction. The 30-year JGB yield rose 2.5bp to 3.865% after the result.

squawks.headline: China's trade surplus tops $1tn in the first 10 months of the year
squawks.detail: The FT and Reuters report China's January to October trade surplus passed $1tn, led by exports of high-tech goods linked to AI infrastructure. Customs data put October exports up 28.7% y/y in yuan terms and imports up 34.7%.

squawks.headline: China's October dollar exports rise 35.2% y/y, above the 33.5% forecast; trade surplus of $105.28bn falls short of $125.8bn poll
squawks.detail: Chinese customs data show October dollar-denominated exports up 35.2% y/y against a poll of 33.5%, with the trade surplus at $105.28bn against a forecast of $125.8bn. The surplus with the United States was $32.71bn, and yuan-denominated exports rose 28.7% y/y.

squawks.headline: Japan offers 0.6 trillion yen of 30-year government bonds with a 4.200% coupon
squawks.detail: Japan's government is offering 0.6 trillion yen of 30-year JGBs carrying a 4.200% coupon. Separately, Finance Minister Katayama said no decision has been taken on tax incentives for retail JGBs and left the debate to the LDP.

squawks.headline: Barclays data show UK consumer spending up 2.3% y/y in October, the most since July 2025, while confidence hits its lowest since April
squawks.detail: Barclays said UK card spending rose 2.3% year on year in October, up from 2.0% in September and the largest increase since July 2025. It also said consumer confidence in October was the weakest since April.

squawks.headline: UK BRC retail sales rise 1.1% y/y, a little below the 1.2% forecast
squawks.detail: The British Retail Consortium's retail sales monitor shows annual growth of 1.1%, against a forecast of 1.2% and up from 1.0% previously.

squawks.headline: BoJ October summary of opinions shows several members favour further rate rises towards neutral
squawks.detail: In the Bank of Japan's October summary of opinions, one member said underlying inflation has reached 2% and the policy rate must reach neutral soon, and one said Japan's neutral rate is likely well above 1%. Other members urged caution, citing some economic weakness and the need to watch financial conditions for several months after each rate rise.

squawks.headline: Japan's September household spending falls 6.8% y/y, a much steeper drop than the 3.1% expected
squawks.detail: Japanese government data show household spending down 6.8% year on year and down 2.8% month on month in September, against a poll forecast of a 0.3% monthly rise.

squawks.headline: Trump tells reporters US military action against Iran does not look necessary for now
squawks.detail: US President Donald Trump told reporters on Monday that US military action against Iran did not currently appear necessary, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: Iran's top security official denies talks with the US are taking place and tells Washington to accept Tehran's seven conditions
squawks.detail: Iran's top security official told the US to stop putting out false reports of talks that he said do not exist. He also said it was time for Washington to give in to the seven conditions Iran has repeatedly set out.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US has another aircraft carrier ready as Iran talks continue
squawks.detail: US President Trump said in remarks on Iran on Monday evening that the US has a further aircraft carrier loaded up. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Qatar's prime minister says he met Trump and Vance to discuss ways to move Iran negotiations forward
squawks.detail: Qatar's prime minister said the meeting with US President Trump and Vice President Vance covered ways to make progress in negotiations with Iran.

squawks.headline: Trump says Iran is effectively finished as a military force and the US is keeping Iran at the status quo
squawks.detail: US President Trump made the remarks on Monday evening, and repeated that he sees momentum towards ending the conflict. The posts in this batch report no market reaction.

squawks.headline: Iran's IRGC navy disables navigation systems of four large oil tankers using an unauthorised Strait of Hormuz route, Press TV says
squawks.detail: Iranian state broadcaster Press TV reports that the Revolutionary Guard navy disabled the navigation systems of four large oil tankers over the past 24 hours, leaving them unable to continue through the Strait of Hormuz. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Trump says he sees positive momentum towards ending the Iran conflict and that an Iranian nuclear weapon is non-negotiable
squawks.detail: In a Truth Social post, US President Trump said all parties agree that Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon. He added that the US stands ready to act if the situation in the Middle East changes, but that this now looks quite unlikely.

squawks.headline: Trump says he had an excellent conversation with Qatar's prime minister
squawks.detail: The US president said this in a Truth Social post. Earlier reports said the talks covered efforts towards a deal with Iran.

squawks.headline: Canada extends tariff relief on goods hit by US tariffs by one year, to 30 June 2028
squawks.detail: Canada's finance minister said the general remission for US tariffs is extended to 30 June 2028. Relief will also cover non-steel goods used in mining, quarrying and oil and gas extraction, and certain imported goods that are in short supply in Canada.

squawks.headline: Arab and Muslim leaders press Trump not to restart war with Iran, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Arab and Muslim leaders are trying to ease tensions, amid fears that the US president will resume hostilities with Iran.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine's gains on the battlefield give Kyiv a stronger hand in peace talks
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said recent battlefield successes have strengthened Kyiv's negotiating position. The remarks come ahead of this week's Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine.

squawks.headline: Trump says this week's Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine offer a chance of a possible breakthrough
squawks.detail: US President Donald Trump said on Monday that the Abu Dhabi talks on the war in Ukraine, due this week, could bring a breakthrough. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Trump says US is prepared to strike Iran if needed, though Qatar and Saudi Arabia favour a peaceful settlement
squawks.detail: Speaking to Reuters after talks with Qatar's leader, US President Trump said Qatar would prefer a peaceful outcome with Iran but the US stands ready to carry out strikes if necessary. He added that Saudi Arabia would also prefer a peaceful solution to the conflict.

squawks.headline: Trump's talks with Qatar's prime minister on Iran deal efforts were positive, a diplomat tells Axios
squawks.detail: Axios cites a diplomat who described the talks between President Trump and Qatar's prime minister as positive. Qatar is helping to mediate between the US and Iran on the details of a deal.

squawks.headline: Brent crude futures settle at $92.57 a barrel, down $5.75 or 5.85% on the day
squawks.detail: Brent futures closed at $92.57 a barrel, $5.75 or 5.85% lower on the session.

squawks.headline: Proposed US-Iran framework would reopen Strait of Hormuz, lift naval blockade and free $6bn-$9bn of Iranian assets, Al Arabiya says
squawks.detail: Al Arabiya sources say the Strait of Hormuz would be opened and the naval blockade lifted immediately under the proposed framework, and the US would release $6 billion to $9 billion of Iranian assets if a deal is reached. The sources also say arrangements are being made to discuss the return of IAEA inspectors to Iran, without setting out the scope of their work.

squawks.headline: US lets Iran enrich uranium at home to 3.67% and Tehran agrees, Al Arabiya sources say; preliminary enrichment deal seen as likely
squawks.detail: Al Arabiya, citing sources, reports that Washington has allowed Iran to enrich uranium domestically to 3.67%, that Tehran has accepted, and that a preliminary agreement on cutting Iran's enrichment is likely. The same sources say arrangements are being made to discuss the return of IAEA inspectors to Iran, without saying what their duties would cover.

squawks.headline: WTI crude December futures settle at $86.85, down $3.98 or 4.38% on the day
squawks.detail: NYMEX WTI December crude futures settled at $86.85 a barrel, a fall of $3.98 or 4.38%. NYMEX natural gas December futures settled at $3.2180/MMBtu.

squawks.headline: Iran says three tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz after using unauthorised routes
squawks.detail: Iran said three tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and footage showed one tanker on fire on the shipping route. The posts report that attacks on commercial shipping are continuing; no market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: OPEC oil output rises in October to 90% of its pre-war level, Reuters survey finds
squawks.detail: A Reuters survey shows OPEC production rose in October, led by gains in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq. Exports remain constrained by the Iran war and a US blockade on Iranian shipments.

squawks.headline: Bank of France expects moderate growth in the French economy in the fourth quarter
squawks.detail: The Bank of France says French economic growth will be moderate in the fourth quarter. It had earlier said it faces great uncertainty in assessing growth.

squawks.headline: Bank of France says it faces great uncertainty in assessing growth
squawks.detail: The Bank of France said there is great uncertainty around its assessment of growth. No figures were reported with the comment.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin calls last jobs report healthy but says firms are still in a low-hire, low-fire mode
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin also said ballot measures approved in recent US elections should not stop data centre expansion because firms will find other places to build. He added that it would help if each Fed policy meeting came with two full months of economic data.

squawks.headline: Zelenskyy tells European partners he expects sustained Russian attacks on Dnipro bridges aimed at splitting Ukraine
squawks.detail: The FT reports that Ukraine's president has warned European partners he expects Russia to launch sustained attacks on bridges across the Dnipro river in an attempt to cut the country in half. The warning comes during the Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin says he has no base case for December and sees policy rate around or slightly below neutral
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said he has no base case for the December meeting and called the last jobs report healthy, though firms remain in a low-hire, low-fire pattern. He also said it is hard to know how the elections will affect the economy.

squawks.headline: US officials say they do not expect the Abu Dhabi talks to end the Ukraine war, only to clarify each side's positions
squawks.detail: US officials told CBS the Abu Dhabi talks aim to get Russia and Ukraine to set out their positions so compromises can be explored later. They also said Washington wants Russia to agree to multilateral negotiations that include Europe.

squawks.headline: Italian cabinet approves a gas price cap to bring down energy bills
squawks.detail: Italy's cabinet has backed a cap on gas prices intended to lower household and business energy bills, according to a market news report.

squawks.headline: US $58bn 3-year note auction prices at 4.627% with a 0.5bp tail; bid-to-cover falls to 2.53
squawks.detail: The US Treasury sold $58bn of 3-year notes at a high yield of 4.627%, against 4.932% at the previous auction, with bid-to-cover of 2.53 compared with 2.62 last time. Indirect bidders took 55.48%, directs 35.04% and primary dealers 9.48%, and 73.41% of bids at the high yield were allotted.

squawks.headline: US 3-year when-issued yield stands at 4.622% ahead of $58bn Treasury auction
squawks.detail: The when-issued 3-year US Treasury yield was 4.622% just before the US Treasury's $58 billion 3-year note auction on Monday.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin says government debt, rather than consumer debt, is at a historically high level
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said in remarks on Monday that government debt, not consumer debt, is at historic levels.

squawks.headline: US official says Washington seeks NATO-like security guarantees for Ukraine and a stronger NATO-Russia Council
squawks.detail: A US official speaking about the Ukraine talks said US security guarantees will be discussed and that Russia is showing positive signs on ending the war. The official also said the US wants to make a NATO-Russia Council more robust.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin calls the US economy remarkably stable, with muted layoffs but bleak consumer sentiment
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said businesses are doing well, with strong earnings, few layoffs and healthy loan pipelines, and that loan demand goes well beyond AI. He said consumer sentiment is bleak but people are still spending because the job market is resilient.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey says policymakers can no longer afford to assume supply shocks will fade
squawks.detail: The Bank of England Governor made the remark in a speech on Monday evening. He said it can no longer be taken for granted that supply shocks will pass on their own.

squawks.headline: US official says Ukraine territorial issues will wait until post-war security architecture is settled; US to press Russia on wider format
squawks.detail: A US official briefing on the Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks said the US will try to get Russia to accept a multilateral format with Europe at the table after the trilateral meeting, and that both parties are coming with good intentions. The official said territorial questions will not be resolved until the post-war security architecture is known.

squawks.headline: US official says European partners will join the Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks and both sides show some private flexibility on territory
squawks.detail: A US official said European partners will take part in the Abu Dhabi talks and that Washington will try to get Russia to accept a multilateral format, with daily contact with both Ukraine and Russia. The official also said Kyiv and Moscow have privately shown a little flexibility on territorial concessions, and that NATO will remain central to European collective defence.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey says UK activity is more resilient than expected, helped by AI investment, but warns an AI asset bubble threatens stability
squawks.detail: In a speech, Bank of England Governor Bailey said there are growing signs of an early positive supply shock from AI and investment, notably in business services. He also said an AI asset price bubble poses clear financial stability risks, as markets could overvalue AI returns, and that frontier AI has raised cyberattack risks.

squawks.headline: NY Fed survey shows Americans growing more worried about the US labour market outlook
squawks.detail: The New York Fed's consumer expectations survey for October, published on Monday, found US households more concerned about future unemployment. No figures for the labour market measures were given in the report.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin reports broad-based cost pressures, with firms planning to pass higher costs on to customers
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said resilient demand and wide-ranging cost increases are pushing prices up, and that businesses are reporting strong earnings while bankers describe healthy loan pipelines. He said layoffs remain muted and consumers keep spending on the back of a resilient job market, even though consumer sentiment is weak.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin says inflation is where the risk lies and policy should move with care despite a clear direction
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said the risk sits on the inflation side of the Fed's mandate. He described the US economy as remarkably stable and said the direction of policy is straightforward but changes should be made with care.

squawks.headline: Brent crude falls to a 10-week low after Trump says US strikes on Iran are highly unlikely
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Brent extended last week's losses, which came after the Republicans' midterm defeat, to reach its lowest level in 10 weeks.
